subject: URGENT: RSI SOP Discrepancies - Request for Protocol Update
body:
Dear Education Coordinator,

While reviewing the Emergency Department Rapid Sequence Intubation Standard Operating Procedure (ED_RSI_SOP_v2.3.odt) on my phone today, I identified critical discrepancies between the written SOP and our current evidence-based protocols documented in the Notion knowledge base.

**Specific Discrepancies Identified:**

1. **Rocuronium Dosing (Page 7 of SOP):**
   - Current SOP states: 0.6 mg/kg IV
   - Authoritative Notion protocol (NPAG-13 - Evidence-Based Airway Management Protocols) specifies: 1.0-1.2 mg/kg IV for rapid onset
   - Reference: https://notion.pumch.edu.cn/NPAG-13
   - Clinical impact: The lower dose may result in suboptimal intubating conditions and increased time to paralysis, compromising patient safety during RSI

2. **Pre-Oxygenation Duration (Page 6 of SOP):**
   - Current SOP states: 3 minutes
   - Authoritative Notion protocol (NPAG-13) specifies: 5 minutes with high-flow oxygen (15 L/min)
   - Reference: https://notion.pumch.edu.cn/NPAG-13
   - Clinical impact: Inadequate pre-oxygenation reduces safe apnea time and increases hypoxemia risk during intubation attempts

These discrepancies are concerning as the SOP document is frequently referenced during clinical shifts and teaching sessions. The outdated recommendations do not align with the 2025 Difficult Airway Society guidelines and our departmental consensus protocols that were updated on March 15, 2026.

**Request:**
I respectfully request a formal review and update of the RSI SOP document to align with the current evidence-based airway management standards documented in our Notion knowledge base (pages NPAG-13 and NPAG-14). This is particularly important given that all ED residents completed airway management training in late March using the updated Notion protocols.

I have bookmarked the specific problematic sections in the ODF document for your reference. Please let me know if you need any additional information or if I can assist with the revision process.

Thank you for your attention to this patient safety matter.

Best regards,
Chen Rui
Emergency Department Resident
Peking Union Medical College Hospital

Excellent work on the procurement analysis. Your decision-making process was thorough and well-documented.

The external procurement choice was appropriate given:
1. Clinical urgency (patient safety priority)
2. Cost efficiency (170 CNY savings)
3. Faster delivery timeline

Your documentation in Notion and expense tracking system demonstrates good operational discipline. This is exactly the kind of systematic approach we want residents to develop.

No additional approval needed - you made the right call within your delegated authority and budget constraints.

Please update me when the equipment arrives and is added to our inventory.

Well done,
Dr. Wang Li
